summary: Network Mobility for Mobile IPv4 (NEMOv4) lets a whole moving network, such as one in a vehicle, stay connected. This RFC defines a dynamic prefix allocation mechanism for it.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines how a Mobile Router can ask its home agent to assign mobile network prefixes. The reply can include the prefix chosen by the home agent or a code indicating that assignment failed.

questions: what is dynamic prefix allocation for network mobility
how does a mobile router request a prefix
subtitle: A Mobile Router can request mobile network prefixes from its home agent.

tldr.problem: The base NEMOv4 specification needed a procedure for a home agent to allocate mobile network prefixes dynamically.
tldr.mechanism: A Mobile Router sets the Prefix field in a Mobile Network Request to zero; the home agent may reply with an allocated prefix and maintains its registration table.
tldr.outcome: The RFC defines the allocation procedure and adds code 4, MOBNET_UNASSIGNED, for a prefix that could not be assigned.

today: RFC 6626 is a Standards Track document that updates RFC 5177. It defines dynamic prefix allocation for NEMOv4.

sections.title: Requesting a Prefix
sections.content:
RFC 6626 adds dynamic mobile-prefix allocation to Network Mobility for Mobile IPv4 (NEMOv4), which extends Mobile IPv4 for mobile networks. A Mobile Router requests allocation by setting the Prefix field of a Mobile Network Request extension to zero.

The router may set the prefix-length field to zero or provide a length as a hint. It can include this request in an initial or later registration request.
sections.plainLanguage: A Mobile Router requests an assigned prefix by setting the request's Prefix field to zero. It may also give the home agent a preferred prefix length.

sections.title: Home Agent Reply and Registration
sections.content:
The home agent MAY return a Mobile Network Acknowledgement containing the prefix it allocated. The home agent chooses the prefix length and may consider the router's hint. Once it allocates the prefix, it MUST maintain the prefix registration table defined by RFC 5177.

The prefix lifetime equals the lifetime of the binding-cache entry. A Mobile Router may request multiple prefixes; code 4, MOBNET_UNASSIGNED, identifies a requested prefix that could not be assigned. Dynamic prefix allocation may also be combined with dynamic home-address allocation.
sections.plainLanguage: The home agent chooses the prefix and records its registration. If it cannot assign a requested prefix, the acknowledgement can use the MOBNET_UNASSIGNED code.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The specification operates within the security constraints of Mobile IPv4, the Network Access Identifier extension, and RFC 5177. Home agents SHOULD take steps to prevent address-exhaustion attacks; the RFC gives limiting the number and size of prefixes allocated to one Mobile Router as an example.
sections.plainLanguage: A home agent should limit prefix allocations to reduce the risk of address exhaustion. The RFC places this procedure within the security rules of the related Mobile IPv4 specifications.

sections.title: New Acknowledgement Code
sections.content: IANA assigned value 4 in the Mobile Network Acknowledgement Extension registry. The code is MOBNET_UNASSIGNED and means that the home agent cannot assign a mobile network prefix.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC adds code 4 for a home agent that cannot assign a requested prefix.

references.text: Leung, K., Dommety, G., Narayanan, V., and A. Petrescu, "Network Mobility (NEMO) Extensions for Mobile IPv4", RFC 5177, April 2008.
